examples.text: Ладно, говори прямо, чего ты хочешь?
examples.trans: All right, speak plainly, what do you want?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Теперь она не хочет со мной разговаривать.
examples.trans: Now she does not want to speak with me.

examples.text: Ты хотел меня специально вчера споить!
examples.trans: You wanted to get me drunk on purpose!

examples.text: Катя совсем не хочет меня видеть.
examples.trans: Katya does not want to see me at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Смотри, у нас на столе закуска.
examples.trans: Look, we have snacks on the table.

examples.text: Смотри, вот я захожу к тебе!
examples.trans: Look, here I am walking in to see you!

examples.text: Я вообще ничего не собираюсь смотреть!
examples.trans: I am not going to watch anything at all!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'положить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Смотри, я кладу флешку в печку.
examples.trans: Look, I am putting the flash drive into the microwave.

examples.text: Постой, не клади трубку!
examples.trans: Wait, don't hang up!

examples.text: Куда ты кладёшь ключи?
examples.trans: Where do you put the keys?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'drive', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Смотри, я кладу флешку в печку.
examples.trans: Look, I am putting the flash drive into the microwave.

examples.text: Алло, Дима, зайди в мой кабинет.
examples.trans: Hello, Dima, step into my office.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Смотри, я кладу флешку в печку.
examples.trans: Look, I am putting the flash drive into the microwave.

examples.text: Даже печку поставить не могут.
examples.trans: They can't even put a heater in.

examples.text: В доме тёплая печка.
examples.trans: There is a warm stove in the house.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'dirty', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Я не хочу грязной победы, Дима.
examples.trans: I do not want a dirty victory, Dima.

examples.text: Унитаз грязный.
examples.trans: The toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Какой грязный пол!
examples.trans: What a dirty floor!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'victory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я не хочу грязной победы, Дима.
examples.trans: I do not want a dirty victory, Dima.

examples.text: Люди аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People applaud your victory!

examples.text: День великой Победы.
examples.trans: The day of great Victory.
